rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data, so this is a baseline built from the contract rather than from telemetry. Geometry: five sensors spread across the 25 mm tape at x = -0.02, -0.01, 0, 0.01, 0.02 m, all at y = 0.04 m ahead of the axle. Five sensors cover roughly ±2 cm, so the line stays visible on moderate errors, and 12 mm footprints overlap the 25 mm tape enough to give a smooth reading. Wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body width 0.12 m (off-track limit about 0.06 m, the same as the floor), body length 0.16 m, mass 0.8 kg are mid-range values that give a stable yaw inertia. Controller: sensor weights are the sensor x positions scaled to cm (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the signal is roughly the lateral offset in cm and stays within ±2. kp = 2.5 gives about 875 PWM of differential per cm of error, which is firm but not saturating. kd = 0.2 damps the oscillation a proportional-only loop would show at this speed. ki = 0.02 is small to avoid integral windup on curves. base_speed = 1.5 targets about 1.5 m/s average, the minimum needed to finish in 3 s, with headroom for slowdowns in bends. line_loss = last_direction keeps the robot turning toward the side it last saw the line when it drops off a bend. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with rms error well under 0.03 m. The slalom is the risk: at this speed the loop may oscillate or lose the line on sharp direction changes. Hypotheses to test: (1) kp is near the stability limit, so steering_oscillation rises if kd is too low; (2) base_speed 1.5 is the largest value that completes within 3 s without line loss; (3) line_loss_events stays at 0 if the sensor spread covers the tape at the speeds used.
